summary: "I’m Still Here: The Story of Eagle" is an interactive, educational single-page web application designed for young explorers aged 9 to 14. It tells the story of the historic 1969 Apollo 11 Moon landing from the first-person perspective of "Eagle" (Lunar Module LM-5)—specifically its descent stage, which remains at Tranquility Base today. By blending first-person storytelling with verified archival data from NASA’s National Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA), the project transforms static technical records into an accessible, engaging digital experience. Users can explore Eagle's technical specifications, step through an interactive landing timeline, inspect a to-scale SVG map of the Apollo 11 neighborhood, learn how the Early Apollo Scientific Experiment Package (EASEP) operated on the lunar surface, and test their knowledge with an interactive quiz. This project makes space history and lunar science tangible and memorable for the next generation of explorers.
details:
"I’m Still Here: The Story of Eagle" takes users on a guided, first-person journey to coordinates 0.67416° N, 23.47314° E in the Sea of Tranquility. Speaking directly as the Apollo 11 Lunar Module descent stage, the application walks students aged 9–14 through six interactive learning modules:

  • 1. Technical Anatomy ("What I am"): Breaks down the two-stage design of LM-5, highlighting key figures such as its 15,103 kg launch mass, 8,248 kg descent fuel capacity, and 9.4 m footpad span.
  • 2. Interactive Mission Timeline ("The landing"): An interactive, tab-driven timeline tracking eight critical milestones from undocking (17:44 UT, July 20, 1969) and the 756.3-second descent engine burn to touchdown (20:17:40 UT), moonwalk sample collection (21.55 kg), and liftoff.
  • 3. To-Scale Landing Site Map ("Explore my neighborhood"): An interactive vector (SVG) map drawn to scale (1 grid step = 25 m) showing the astronauts' 100 m maximum walking radius and clickable hotspots for Eagle's descent stage, the EASEP science station (17 m south), and the Laser Ranging Retroreflector.
  • 4. EASEP Science Station Explorer: Interactive component cards detailing the solar panels, passive seismometer, dust detector, isotope heater, radio frequencies (2119 MHz / 2276.5 MHz), and thermal survival data across the lunar day.
  • 5. Post-Mission Fate & Legacy: Explains how the descent stage served as a launch pad and why the passive laser retroreflector continues to function today without electricity.
  • 6. Interactive Memory Quiz: A 4-question self-grading quiz with instant feedback to reinforce student comprehension.

How It Works & Tools Used:

  • Languages & Architecture: Built as a lightweight, zero-dependency, single-file web application using semantic HTML5, modern CSS3 (custom properties, responsive CSS Grid/Flexbox, automatic light/dark mode support via prefers-color-scheme, and reduced-motion accessibility), and vanilla JavaScript.
  • Graphics & Typography: Uses inline scalable vector graphics (SVG) for crisp, resolution-independent mapping and Google Fonts (Bricolage Grotesque and Atkinson Hyperlegible) to maximize readability and accessibility for young readers and visually impaired users.

Benefits & Goals: Because the entire experience is self-contained in a single lightweight HTML file, it loads instantaneously even on low-bandwidth connections and runs offline in any browser. Our goal is to bridge the gap between complex archival NASA mission data and youth STEM education through empathy-driven storytelling.
